findings.evidence: Rule check: 4 channel(s) not assigned to a sample: TMT132C, TMT133N, TMT133C, TMT134N. Description: "Four channels are unused."
findings.explanation: 12 samples use TMT126 to TMT132N of the 16 TMTpro channels, leaving 4 empty. This matches the description (12 samples in a 16-plex kit), so the empty channels are expected. They carry no sample information and have no effect on the analysis, apart from slightly lower multiplexing.
findings.suggested_fix: No change needed. Optionally note in the metadata that TMT132C, TMT133N, TMT133C and TMT134N were intentionally left empty.

findings.evidence: Description: "RL cells (human diffuse large B-cell lymphoma cell line)"; SDRF characteristics[cell line]: HEK293 (while cellosaurus name is RL and accession is CVCL_1660)
findings.explanation: The cell line is recorded as HEK293, but the experiment used RL cells. HEK293 is a human embryonic kidney line, which also contradicts the disease column (diffuse large B-cell lymphoma) and the cellosaurus name (RL) in the same SDRF.
findings.suggested_fix: Change characteristics[cell line] to RL in all rows, and check that the cellosaurus accession matches RL.

summary: The one rule issue (4 unused channels) matches the description and is expected. One real mismatch: the cell line is listed as HEK293, but the description and the other SDRF columns (cellosaurus name, disease) indicate RL cells.
